title: Scope: the formal core of Brouwer degree, on real Mathlib homology
content: The header fixes exactly what is proved and what is assumed. The Brouwer degree of a self-map f : Sⁿ → Sⁿ is the integer by which f acts on the top homology Hₙ(Sⁿ) ≅ ℤ. Its four defining properties — deg(id)=1, multiplicativity, degree ±1 for homeomorphisms, and identification-independence — are purely formal consequences of homology being a functor plus Hₙ(Sⁿ)≅ℤ. This file isolates that formal content (0 sorries, 0 axioms) on Mathlib's genuine singular-homology functor (Andrew Yang, 2025). The one input Mathlib cannot yet supply, Hₙ(Sⁿ)≅ℤ, is kept as an explicit hypothesis e — never an axiom — so every theorem has the honest conditional shape.
mathContext: $\deg f$ is the integer with $f_* = (\cdot\,\deg f)$ on $H_n(S^n)\cong\mathbb{Z}$.

title: Building on Mathlib's genuine homology functor
content: The imports pull in Mathlib's singular homology theory (SingularHomology.Basic) and the category AddCommGrpCat of abelian groups together with its abelian/colimit structure. Crucially this is the real homology functor, not a toy model: working through TopCat ⥤ AddCommGrpCat means the degree machinery here is directly compatible with whatever future Mathlib lemmas establish Hₙ(Sⁿ)≅ℤ.

title: Degree of an endomorphism through an identification with ℤ
content: The algebraic seed of the whole development. Given an abelian group G with a chosen isomorphism e : G ≃+ ℤ and an endomorphism f : G →+ G, the degree is defined as the integer e(f(e⁻¹ 1)) — the image of the generator under the conjugate of f to ℤ. Because every additive endomorphism of ℤ is multiplication by a fixed integer, this single number completely determines the conjugated map.
mathContext: $\deg_e f := e\bigl(f(e^{-1}(1))\bigr) \in \mathbb{Z}$; the conjugate $e\circ f\circ e^{-1}$ is multiplication by this integer.

title: The characterizing property: conjugation is multiplication by the degree
content: This lemma is the workhorse the rest of the file leans on. It shows the conjugate map n ↦ e(f(e⁻¹ n)) is exactly multiplication by deg(f), for every n — not just at the generator. The proof packages the composite e ∘ f ∘ e⁻¹ as a single AddMonoidHom ℤ →+ ℤ and invokes ℤ-linearity (map_zsmul): any such map is determined by its value at 1, which is by definition the degree.
mathContext: $e(f(e^{-1}(n))) = (\deg_e f)\cdot n$ for all $n\in\mathbb{Z}$, since an additive map $\mathbb{Z}\to\mathbb{Z}$ is $n\mapsto c\,n$ with $c$ its value at $1$.

title: Multiplicativity: deg(g∘f) = deg(g)·deg(f)
content: The algebraic form of the degree's headline functoriality property. deg(id)=1 is immediate from the definition. For composition, the proof rewrites f(e⁻¹ 1) as e⁻¹(deg f) and then applies the conjugation identity for g at n = deg(f), turning e(g(e⁻¹(deg f))) into deg(g)·deg(f). This is where 'the conjugate is multiplication by the degree' pays off: composition of self-maps becomes multiplication of integers.

title: Well-definedness: the degree is independent of the identification
content: The subtle correctness theorem. A priori deg depends on the chosen iso e : G ≃+ ℤ; this proves any two choices e₁, e₂ give the same integer. The argument transports through the change-of-identification automorphism ψ = e₂ ∘ e₁⁻¹ : ℤ →+ ℤ, which sends the relevant generator a ↦ 1, and uses its ℤ-linearity to peel off the scalar d. Conceptually this is the commutativity (centrality) of integer multiplication: changing basis on ℤ cannot change a scalar.
mathContext: $\deg_{e_1} f = \deg_{e_2} f$; the change-of-identification map $\psi=e_2\circ e_1^{-1}$ is $\mathbb{Z}$-linear, so the scalar is conjugation-invariant.

title: Automorphisms have degree ±1
content: For an automorphism σ : G ≃+ G the degrees of σ and σ⁻¹ multiply to deg(id)=1 (by multiplicativity), so deg(σ) is a unit of ℤ. Since the only units of ℤ are ±1 (Int.isUnit_iff), an automorphism has degree exactly +1 or -1. Applied to a homeomorphism this recovers the classical fact that a self-homeomorphism of Sⁿ has degree ±1.

title: The degree's properties ARE the functor laws
content: Section II reveals the conceptual punchline: for an arbitrary functor F : C ⥤ AddCommGrpCat, functorDegree transports the algebraic degree through F. Then functorDegree_id is literally F.map_id and functorDegree_comp is literally F.map_comp, fed through Section I. So deg(id)=1 and deg(g∘f)=deg(g)·deg(f) are not analytic facts about spheres — they are the two functor axioms read through End(F.obj X) ≅ ℤ. Note the reversed composition order (f ≫ g) tracking covariant functoriality.
mathContext: $F.\mathrm{map}(\mathrm{id})=\mathrm{id}$ and $F.\mathrm{map}(f\gg g)=F.\mathrm{map}\,f\gg F.\mathrm{map}\,g$ become $\deg(\mathrm{id})=1$ and multiplicativity.

title: Isomorphisms map to automorphisms, hence degree ±1
content: An iso σ : X ≅ X in C is sent by F to an iso F.mapIso σ in AddCommGrpCat; addCommGroupIsoToAddEquiv turns that categorical isomorphism into a genuine additive automorphism of F.obj X, to which degreeOfEnd_equiv_eq applies. This is the abstract template later instantiated to 'homeomorphisms have Brouwer degree ±1'.
mathContext: $F$ sends an iso to an iso; an automorphism of $\mathbb{Z}$ has degree $\pm1$.

title: Instantiation: the real Brouwer degree on singular homology
content: Section III plugs Mathlib's actual functor into Section II. Hn n is the n-th integral singular homology functor Hₙ(-;ℤ) : TopCat ⥤ AddCommGrpCat, obtained by applying singularHomologyFunctor to the coefficient object ℤ. brouwerDegree is functorDegree of Hn, with brouwerDegree_id, brouwerDegree_comp, and brouwerDegree_iso_eq (homeomorphisms have degree ±1) inherited verbatim from the functorial layer. The ContinuousMap wrappers brouwerDegreeCM/_id repackage continuous self-maps C(α,α) through TopCat for ergonomic use. Every result still carries the explicit identification hypothesis e : Hₙ(X) ≃+ ℤ.
